homonyms.basis: the MMRS record carries no disambiguation for the entity, and no card on the rail is another entity of the name: all six are MIT's own surfaces. The parent and neighbours are distinct entities, kept as relations, never senses of the name: the MIT AI Risk Repository (part_of; Wikipedia's one mention credits the tracker's classification to it, F53), the AI Incident Database (derived_from), the MIT AI Risk Navigator (a separate MIT project that presents the tracker's data, B5), and the databases the June 2026 update names beside it (the OECD's AI Incident Monitor, the AIAAIC Repository, the Political Deepfakes Database, F31).

captures.description: THE MIT AI INCIDENT TRACKER, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'an interactive tool developed by the MIT AI Risk Initiative that classifies and analyzes real-world artificial intelligence mishaps'; it processes AI Incident Database reports 'using automated large language model (LLM) pipelines', rates harm on a 1–5 scale, sorts by the repository's domains, adds national-security views, and is browsable in the Risk Navigator. Six cards, all MIT's; the first card's summary says it 'classifies 1,752 real-world AI incident reports'.
